items.notes: Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Gochujang' to USDA FNDDS 'Hoisin sauce' through an exact retained record in the same immutable evidence snapshot. Gochujang is a thick sweet-salty fermented Korean chili paste containing pepper, grain/starch, and fermented soy, while hoisin is a thick sweet-salty fermented soybean-based sauce; the pinned hoisin profile is therefore a reasonable nutrient-profile surrogate for energy, carbohydrate, sugar, and sodium. Confidence remains medium because gochujang's chili content, fermentation, protein, salt, and brand formulation differ; this decision does not generalize to plain chili sauce, soy sauce, miso, sriracha, or diluted gochujang dishes.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Ras el hanout' to USDA SR Legacy 'Spices, curry powder' through an exact retained record in the same immutable evidence snapshot. Ras el hanout and curry powder are both dry multi-spice blends used in small seasoning quantities, so curry powder is the closest pinned composite-spice profile available. Confidence remains medium because the component spices and proportions vary substantially by region and brand; this decision does not generalize to curry paste, single spices, fresh herbs, or wet marinades.
